from.place: projective presentation and resolution splicing in the successor induction step

title: Splicing a projective presentation
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, n a natural number, and S a short exact complex in ModuleCat.{v} R. If S.X₂ is categorical-projective and S.X₁ has a projective resolution of length at most n [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then S.X₃ has a projective resolution of length at most n+1.

proof.text: Given a bounded resolution P of S.X₁, augment its complex by S.X₂ using P.π.f 0 followed by S.f. Augment to S.X₃ by S.g. Exactness in degree zero follows from S.exact and epimorphy of P.π.f 0; exactness in degree one follows from P.exact₀ and monomorphy of S.f. Higher degrees use P.exact_succ. The augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by the exact-and-epi criterion in degree zero and the exactAt criterion in positive degrees. Terms are projective and all degrees above n+1 vanish by the bound on P.

mathlib_searches.query: If the kernel of a short exact sequence has a projective resolution of length n and the middle term is projective, then the quotient has a projective resolution of length n+1

lean.statement:
theorem hasProjectiveResolutionLE_of_shortExact_projective_middle
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ)
    (S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hproj : Projective S.X₂)
    (hker : HasProjectiveResolutionLE S.X₁ n) :
    HasProjectiveResolutionLE S.X₃ (n + 1)
